details: CONFIRMED by reading: git grep shows relay_plugin_links / real_files used in tests only by tests/test_plugin_links.py, which calls
real_files itself; the PaidPart tests run plugin_evals on a temp root with no plugins/ folder, so the swap is a no-op there and
nothing asserts it happened. The brief asks for a test that fails before the fix "when the plugin folder is used the way the eval
uses it"; the module test covers the swap, not that the eval step uses it. The Recorder pattern of
test_the_old_results_file_is_removed_before_the_eval_step already observes the tree at the moment claude starts, so the test is
cheap. Principle 2 (waste): a paid run that goes red for a cause a free test could catch repeats per wave. Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: tests/test_ci_python.py:106-116 PaidPart.ci(): root is a bare temp folder, lib_links stubbed, no plugins/ folder
failing_case: Remove `with relay_plugin_links.real_files(self.root):` from Ci.plugin_evals (lib/relay_ci.py:431), leaving the bare
self.run(argv, ...). Today: tests/test_plugin_links.py and tests/test_ci_python.py all pass (the only callers of real_files in
tests call it directly; no test runs plugin_evals over a tree with plugin lib links). The regression shows up only as a red
paid run (dollars and about an hour), the very failure this change fixes. Should: a free test fails.
fix_hint: Add a PaidPart test in tests/test_ci_python.py: write lib/relay_x.py and a relative link plugins/p/lib/relay_x.py into self.root,
record os.path.islink of the link inside the Recorder answer for argv[0] == "claude", assert False there and True after.
pass_cases: 1. A PaidPart test whose root holds lib/relay_x.py and plugins/p/lib/relay_x.py -> ../../../lib/relay_x.py: while the stub
`claude` call runs (the Recorder answer for argv[0] == "claude"), plugins/p/lib/relay_x.py is a regular file with the content
of lib/relay_x.py. Fails when the real_files block is removed from plugin_evals.
2. Same root: after plugin_evals returns, plugins/p/lib/relay_x.py is a link again with its old link text.
3. The existing PaidPart tests (root with no plugins/ folder) keep passing unchanged.
reason: tests/test_plugin_links.py:89 asserts a real file during the claude call and link back after.
findings.summary: no test checks that the eval step runs with real files: dropping the real_files block in relay_ci keeps every test green and only a paid run shows it

details: CONFIRMED by reading lines 33-45: done.append happens after copyfile, so a failure between os.remove and the append is never
undone. SIGTERM/SIGHUP are safe (main() raises on them, the finally runs); SIGKILL is not. Today all links are .py modules, so
(c) is only fragility. Correct today in ordinary use, hence LOW. Size: 5 minutes for (a) and (c) (append before the copy;
evidence: lib/relay_plugin_links.py:36-40: source = realpath; os.remove(path); shutil.copyfile(source, path); done.append((path, text))
failing_case: a) shutil.copyfile raises after os.remove(path) (disk full, permission): `done` has no entry for path, so the finally block does not
recreate the link; the worktree has lost a tracked file (git status: D plugins/relay/lib/relay_toml.py).
b) bin/ci is killed with SIGKILL during the eval (about an hour): no finally runs; every plugin lib link stays a real copy
(git status: T for 35 files), a later gate in that worktree refuses it as not clean, `git worktree remove` needs --force.
c) copyfile drops the mode bits: a future link to an executable (a plugin bin linked to bin/) would become non-executable.
Should: (a) the link comes back whatever step failed; (b)/(c) are noted risks of the in-place design.
fix_hint: Append (path, text) to done before os.remove; use shutil.copy2 (or copyfile + copymode).
pass_cases: 1. real_files over a root where copyfile fails on the second link: on exit every link exists with its old text.
2. The current tests of tests/test_plugin_links.py keep passing (links back after a normal exit and after an exception).
3. A link to an executable target is, inside the block, a file with the target's mode.
reason: tests/test_plugin_links.py:112 and :121 pass (failed copy restores link, mode kept). SIGKILL risk remains, noted by fixer.
findings.summary: the swap edits the gated worktree for the whole eval and is fragile on the way back: a link removed before a failed copy is never restored, and a SIGKILL leaves every link a real file
